source: NASA Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI)
measurementPoint: Sun-Earth L1 Lagrange Point (1.5 million km sunward of Earth)
radiationModelingNote: NASA measures energetic solar proton and X-ray flux in heliocentric space. ASTRA simulation models surface absorption and regolith shielding attenuation (2.5m regolith attenuates 99.4% of ionizing proton dose).

events.name: May 2024 G5 Solar Superstorm (Historic SDO Record)
events.instruments: SDO AIA 131/171, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES-16 SUVI
events.description: One of the most intense space weather superstorms in modern history. A series of cannibal CMEs and multiple X-class solar flares collided to produce an extreme G5 geomagnetic disturbance.
events.operationalRelevance: High ionizing radiation flux in unshielded space. Junior astronauts must halt all extravehicular activities (EVA) and shelter inside the regolith-shielded habitat. Solar arrays face particle sputtering.
events.kidSummary: 🚀 ALERT! The Sun threw a massive giant burst of plasma called an X8.7 solar flare straight at us! Inside our habitat's thick lunar regolith dirt roof, you are completely safe. On Earth, this caused northern lights all the way to tropical latitudes!

events.name: Active Region SDO M2.5 Flare & Fast CME
events.description: A prominent M-class solar flare with a sustained coronal mass ejection heading toward the inner solar system.
events.operationalRelevance: Increased UV and X-ray radiance boosts solar panel efficiency by 15%. Minor radio interference. Short EVAs permitted with strict dosimeter monitoring.
events.kidSummary: ⚡ The Sun is sparkling with medium-sized M-class solar flares! Our solar power generation increases, but junior astronauts must stay within 200 meters of the airlock.

events.name: Solar Minimum / Quiet Sun (Nominal Artemis Baseline)
events.description: Quiet solar conditions with minimal magnetic turbulence. Nominal space weather environment.
events.operationalRelevance: Safe baseline for planetary surface operations, rover geological surveys, and greenhouse biological cultivation.
events.kidSummary: ☀️ Clear skies in space! The Sun is quiet and steady. Perfect weather for long moonwalks, rock sampling, and science experiments!
